note.text: Globalisation is increasing interconnection across borders through goods, services, finance, people and information. It has historical roots; recent networks can intensify links without making distance or borders disappear. Production stages may take place in different countries. Opportunities and risks are uneven because capabilities, bargaining power, access and exposure differ.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to trace a cross-border connection and explain an uneven effect. Builds on: transport and communication systems. Leads to: telecommunication networks and trade.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Globalisation is increasing interconnection across borders through goods, services, finance, people and information. It has historical roots; recent networks can intensify links without making distance or borders disappear. Production stages may take place in different countries. Opportunities and risks are uneven because capabilities, bargaining power, access and exposure differ.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: An invented Douala clothing business receives designs electronically, imports fabric, sews garments locally and sells some abroad. Information and physical goods use different networks in the same value chain. A delayed imported input can interrupt local work; a wider market can also create opportunities. Neither outcome applies identically to every firm.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Draw the production stages, places and connecting flows. Explain a benefit and a vulnerability using this chain. Distinguish global interconnection from equal outcomes or an absence of rules and borders.

pick.q: An invented workshop receives designs online and fabric by ship. Which explanation fits?
pick.r: Different networks connect information and materials in one production chain
w: The online design replaces the fabric
The ship transports the design only
Borders have physically disappeared
e: Production still needs material inputs.
The stated ship carries fabric.
Connections do not remove national borders.
pick.y: Trace each actual flow rather than treating them as identical.

w: All international trade always stops production
Local workers caused every foreign delay
Every imported input is unnecessary
e: One case does not prove a universal effect.
The evidence identifies a supplier delay.
The process may depend on that input.
pick.y: A linked chain can transmit a specific disruption.

pick.q: A small firm reaches new overseas buyers but faces strong competition. What is justified?
pick.r: Global links create opportunities with uneven outcomes
w: Every firm gains equally
Competition disappears across borders
No transport or payment arrangements are needed
e: Capabilities and costs differ.
Wider markets can increase competition.
Actual exchange still needs supporting arrangements.
pick.y: Evaluate conditions instead of equating connection with guaranteed success.
